title: Use of Health Improvement Card by Chinese Physical Therapy Students: A Pilot Study
author: Alice YM YM YM Jones
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.54kg8uw

steps.title: Recruit Participants
steps.instruction: Recruit physical therapy students from two universities in Shanghai, China.

steps.title: Collect Initial Health Data
steps.instruction: Have students complete the 2-page Chinese version of the Health Improvement Card (HIC) and record physical measurements.

substeps.instruction: Measure waist circumference and blood pressure.

steps.title: Assess Initial Perceptions
steps.instruction: Administer a questionnaire regarding the perceptions of the use and usefulness of the HIC.

substeps.instruction: Have students rate 7 statements using a 4-point Likert scale.

steps.title: Practice HIC Administration
steps.instruction: Have students act as health professionals by administering the HIC to a friend or relative.

substeps.instruction: Invite a friend or relative to complete the HIC.
Return completed HICs to the investigators within one week.

steps.title: Collect Feedback on Administration
steps.instruction: Administer a second questionnaire to obtain feedback on the experience of administering the HIC.

substeps.instruction: Have students answer three open-ended questions regarding positive aspects and challenges encountered during the process.

description: Introduction of the Health Improvement Card (HIC) to physical therapy students from two universities in Shanghai via a standardized 45-min tutorial. Content of the tutorial follows the User Guide for administering the HIC; both of which were developed by the World Health Professions Alliance (www.whpa.org/ncd_health_improvement_card_professionals.pdf).
